RuBisCO. Ribulose-one-five-bisphosphate carboxylase slash oxygenase, the most abundant enzyme on Earth and the catalyst for the first committed step of the Calvin cycle, fixing carbon dioxide into organic molecules. It is a bifunctional enzyme with both carboxylase and oxygenase activity, the latter initiating photorespiration, a competing pathway that reduces photosynthetic efficiency. RuBisCO catalyzes the carboxylation of ribulose-one-five-bisphosphate, abbreviated RuBP, with carbon dioxide, producing two molecules of three-phosphoglycerate. It is located in the stroma of chloroplasts and comprises approximately forty to fifty percent of soluble protein in chloroplasts. It is the most prevalent protein in most plant leaves. The substrate is ribulose-one-five-bisphosphate, a five-carbon sugar, and carbon dioxide, though the enzyme also competes with and can react with oxygen. The product, three-phosphoglycerate, enters glycolysis and gluconeogenesis pathways and feeds the Calvin cycle to produce glucose. When RuBisCO's oxygenase activity activates, it consumes oxygen and generates two-phosphoglycolate, a metabolic dead end that wastes ATP and NADPH. The enzyme is relatively slow, catalyzing approximately one carbon dioxide fixation per second per enzyme molecule, which means huge amounts are needed for sufficient metabolic flux. Light-dependent mechanisms activate the enzyme, and accumulation of RuBP in darkness inactivates it. RuBisCO is the gateway to the biosphere. Nearly all carbon fixation for life on Earth passes through this single enzyme. Its abundance reflects not catalytic perfection but biological necessity. Despite being inefficient by enzyme standards, cells must compensate with enormous quantities. The enzyme's oxygenase activity diverts fixed carbon away from productive pathways, representing an evolutionary compromise. RuBisCO cannot discriminate well between carbon dioxide and oxygen at the catalytic site, and this limitation persists because improving specificity would require redesign that natural selection has not favored.
